# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

For most people I'd get the **Bluetti Elite 200 V2** (about $854 with a code). If you want room to expand later, get the **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2**. These are reviewer rankings and spec sheets, not my own testing.

## Top picks

**1. Bluetti Elite 200 V2: best overall for a single-unit backup**
- It has 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W output, and a LiFePO4 battery rated for 6,000 cycles. Outage Outfitter ranks it #1 for most battery under $1,000 ([source](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/)).
- Price is $899. The code AFF5OFF takes it to $854.05 (tested 10/25) ([source](https://dealectric.com/)).
- **[Buy the Bluetti Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**
- Downsides: it can't be expanded, and one reviewer saw it at $1,199 in early October after a promo ended ([source](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)). The more recent listings show $899, but check the price at checkout.

**2. Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2: best if you want to expand later**
- It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and takes add-on batteries. It costs about $900 ([source](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)).
- The search results didn't include a direct purchase link. Outage Outfitter's page links to the Amazon listing: [Best under $1,000](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/).

**3. Bluetti AC180: best budget pick**
- It has 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W for $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF ([source](https://dealectric.com/)). That's enough for roughly 13 hours of fridge, CPAP, and router ([source](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)).
- **[Buy the Bluetti AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)**
- It weighs 35.3 lb.

**4. Jackery Explorer 1000 v2: best lightweight pick**
- It has 1,070 Wh and 1,500 W, weighs 23.8 lb, and costs $489 at Outbound Power. Jackery's own store raised its price to $559 ([source](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)).
- It has only 400 W of solar input and can't be expanded.
- The results gave no direct purchase link, so see the [review page](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2) for the retailer links.

## Worth a look
- **ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro** has 1,451 Wh and 2,400 W. It's $664, or $597.60 with code ALLPOWERS26. I found only the retailer's spec listing, not independent reviews. **[Link](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-1451wh)**
- **Anker SOLIX F1500** has 1,536 Wh for $599.99, and Compare Power Stations scores it highest for value ([source](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/)). No buy link was in the results.

## Before you buy
- **Size it to your load.** A fridge, CPAP, and router average about 77 W, so a 2 kWh unit covers roughly 23 hours and a 1 kWh unit about 12 ([source](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)). A window AC or space heater needs the higher-output models.
- **Plug-in only.** These run appliances through their outlets and don't power your whole house. For that you'd need a transfer switch and a much larger system.
- **Disclosure:** The Dealectric links are affiliate links. The brand pays them a commission, and it costs you nothing extra. Enter the code at checkout, and the store's final price is what counts.

Tell me what you need to run (fridge, CPAP, window AC) and how long, and I can narrow it to one.
